claims.text: A machine-learning model can optimize sintering parameters such as heating rate, dwell time, and applied pressure.
Machine-learning-optimized sintering can achieve full densification at lower peak temperatures.
Powder-based ceramic or alloy precursors normally require high-temperature conventional sintering for densification.
SPS can be used to process mechanically alloyed elemental powders.
An ML-predicted sintering cycle can combine a lower peak temperature with tailored pressure and heating profiles.
Rapid heating and pressure assistance under a controlled atmosphere can be implemented using SPS.
The time-temperature profile and applied pressure mediate microstructural evolution and densification during sintering.
Optimized sintering parameters reduce the thermal input needed for densification.
Rapid heating and applied pressure accelerate densification kinetics.
Non-intuitive parameter combinations identified by machine learning promote effective nucleation and shrinkage.
Machine-learning-identified parameter combinations limit grain growth.
The optimized process will lower the sintering temperature.
The optimized process will maintain densification and microstructural integrity comparable to conventional high-temperature sintering.
Traditional sintering protocols require prolonged dwell times at elevated temperatures to achieve full densification.
Certain powder-based alloy systems can be processed using SPS.
The proposed temperature-reduction method is applicable to ceramic systems processed by rapid sintering.
The exact reduction in peak temperature and the transferability of optimized parameters across material systems are uncertain.
A controlled comparison of identically composed samples processed by conventional and ML-optimized cycles can test the hypothesis.
Peak temperature, density, microstructure, and mechanical properties are measurable comparison outcomes.
Failure to significantly reduce peak temperature, or degradation of densification, microstructure, or mechanical properties, would falsify the hypothesis.
